name: hyp-37-half
comment: HALF THE {3,7} TRIANGLE. In the hyperbolic {3,7} tiling seven triangles meet at every vertex, so each corner is 360/7 degrees; an altitude cuts one into two triangles with angles pi/2, pi/7 and 2pi/7 — 90, 180/7 and 360/7 degrees. Scalene, so CHIRAL, and so the mirror image is its own alphabet symbol; this palette runs only because of the sided-classes repair. Its sides are the {3,7} edge, half of it and the altitude — three edge types — and the edge is EXACTLY twice the half, which is what cosh(2x) = 2cosh(x)^2 - 1 says about the two: cosh(half) = 1.152389 and cosh(edge) = 1.656027 = 2(1.152389)^2 - 1. D=28 because that is the smallest ring holding all three angles: 180/7 = 2 units of 2pi/28, 360/7 = 4, and 90 = 7. They sum to 13 against the 14 a flat triangle would, so the deficit is 1 unit = 90/7 degrees, which is the tile's area.
